title: Make WI-10 installation prompt-first, beginner-safe, and multiplatform
outOfScope: Changing installer, calibration, runtime, security, or capability implementation behavior
Publishing a release, changing release identity, creating a tag, or modifying provider state
Claiming that Xcode, Android SDK, Gradle, Maven, a JDK, a device, or a hosted CI environment is installed or operational without adopter evidence
Claiming that the later comprehensive Japanese assessment has passed
Changing capability statuses without new implementation evidence
Deleting or rewriting immutable archived Work Item evidence
Closing the WI-01 through WI-20 audit, process-issue stage, RFE-ISSUE-082, documentation alignment, release, or plan-cleanup stages

riskAssessment.reason: Installation is the adoption gateway. An incomplete step, unexplained command, unsafe prompt, language gap, or platform overclaim can prevent first-time users from adopting the project or cause an agent to cross a human decision boundary.

executionDecision.reason: The user explicitly approved this corrective and instructed continuous execution. The required content and safety boundaries are concrete and locally verifiable.

preReviewWarnings: A translated summary is not a complete Chinese or Japanese installation guide.
Prompt-first does not mean granting an agent authority to write, commit, push, open or merge a PR, publish, or select unknown project commands without a human checkpoint.
Platform examples must distinguish repository detection from verified toolchain, simulator/device, signing, and hosted-CI evidence.
A short happy path is insufficient: prerequisites, every scaffold and calibration stage, stop/recovery behavior, and final success checks must remain visible to a novice.
Commands may remain only where the human must bootstrap the agent or directly inspect evidence; every retained command must be labeled and explained in plain language.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: docs/getting-started/installation.md, docs/getting-started/installation.zh-CN.md, and docs/getting-started/installation.ja.md exist as complete same-structure guides; Chinese and Japanese are not summaries.

A person with no programming experience can follow the installation hand sequence from prerequisites through final success without needing to infer a missing action, term, expected result, decision, or recovery step.

The primary path is copy-ready agent prompts: the agent first performs read-only discovery, explains findings in plain language, proposes a plan, stops on unknowns or unsafe state, and requests explicit human confirmation before repository writes.

All retained command-line blocks are necessary human bootstrap or evidence checks, carry a conservative command-evidence label, and explain what to copy, what the command does, what success looks like, and what to do on failure.
The guide documents every Installation Wizard choice and generated scaffold category, shows a checkpoint after each phase, and does not claim that creating files alone completes adoption.

The guide explains all ten calibration stages—repository role, language and stack, source boundaries, test boundaries, generated artifacts, critical paths, quality commands, review obligations, risks and unknowns, and adoption readiness—including yes/no, alternative input, unknown, and not-applicable-with-reason answers.

The guide continues through the first governed Work Item, local checks, finish/archive, commit, PR, hosted CI, human review/merge, lifecycle closure, branch cleanup, and final verification while preserving each human authority boundary.

Complete English, Chinese, and Japanese iOS, Android, and Java examples explain project detection, likely configuration choices, test/build command discovery, platform-specific evidence limits, failure stops, and target-project calibration without assuming a toolchain, device, signing setup, or default remote branch.
README and same-language getting-started layers lead users to the complete installation guide and platform examples without duplicating or contradicting the authoritative procedure.

Executable documentation checks and mutation tests fail when a language guide, novice stage, prompt safety boundary, calibration stage, platform example, command explanation, or same-language link is missing.

The instruction-plan-implementation-acceptance trace contains implementation and acceptance evidence for WI10-AUDIT-001 through WI10-AUDIT-004; full local quality, PR/hosted checks, merge, archive, ai-close-work-item, branch deletion, and main synchronization complete before the WI-01 through WI-20 audit resumes.
guidelines: Write for a reader with no programming experience: define every term before use and pair every action with an expected result and failure response.
Prefer a copy-ready agent prompt over a command whenever an agent can safely perform the action under the repository workflow.

Keep prompts fail closed: read-only discovery first, no invented facts, explicit unknowns, plan review before writes, and no commit, push, PR, merge, release, or deletion without the corresponding governed human decision.
Keep English, Chinese, and Japanese structure, section identifiers, safety meaning, links, and completeness aligned.
Map every user-named file and requirement to implementation evidence or an explicit no-change reason.
Do not infer platform capability, tool installation, hosted execution, or production readiness from documentation intent.
Capability Truth Matrix and executable repository evidence remain authoritative for current capability status.

intent.problem: The merged WI-10 documentation is still too difficult to use as an adoption gateway. There is no complete Chinese installation.md equivalent, the guides expose command lines where copy-ready prompts should be the primary path, iOS/Android/Java walkthroughs are absent, and scaffold/calibration/lifecycle steps are not detailed enough for a person with no programming experience. Because installation difficulty directly prevents promotion, the prior completion claim must be corrected before release.
constraints: Preserve the repository's one-Work-Item/one-branch/one-PR lifecycle and human authority boundaries.
Do not alter runtime or installer behavior in a documentation corrective.
Do not claim platform tools, devices, signing, hosted CI, or enterprise controls have been verified without evidence.
Do not weaken or omit content in Chinese or Japanese.
Keep command-line usage minimal but do not hide commands that a human must execute to bootstrap the process or inspect direct evidence.
Continue the approved serial plan only after this corrective is fully merged and closed.
intent.rationale: A prompt-first, checkpointed, multilingual hand sequence reduces the largest adoption barrier while executable structure and mutation checks prevent the same omissions from being archived as complete again.

rawUserRequest: Correct WI-10 before release. Add a complete Chinese installation guide; use prompts wherever possible because command lines are difficult to understand; add iOS, Android, and Java examples; make installation extremely simple but document every scaffold step, the complete calibration checklist, and the entire governed lifecycle so that a person with no programming experience can install successfully. This is critical to adoption. The user has authorized continuous execution without another confirmation unless a genuine human decision is required.
